data.cultural_impact: The name "Subh" holds immense significance in Islamic culture, as it is the Arabic word for dawn or the early hours of the morning. This time is considered precious and sacred in Islam, as it is believed that Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) used to make duas (prayers) extensively in these hours. Consequently, many Muslims strive to wake up early to perform optional prayers and begin their day with the remembrance of Allah.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Subh" represents the concept of bringing light, both internally and externally. It is a reminder of the guidance and illumination that comes from Allah and a call to be the source of light and positivity in the world. Moreover, it signifies the responsibility to spread love, forgiveness, and kindness to others, just as the sun spreads light and warmth to everyone, regardless of their race, religion, or background.
